subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular POSIX installer architecture now, or keep scripts/install.sh as a single served script while accepting only narrow installer refactors tied to concrete bugs?
rationale: The request changes the structure of a public setup surface whose docs, website sync, tests, and release validation currently assume one script, so automation should not choose the architecture unilaterally.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve an incremental module layout only if the public served installer remains a single safe entrypoint and the website sync plus installer smoke matrix are updated in the same plan.

options.title: Keep focused refactors only
options.body: Leave this as backlog context and continue extracting or deleting small installer sections only when tied to concrete installer bugs or validation improvements.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide that the public shell installer should stay monolithic to reduce helper-loading and curl-piped packaging risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded split
recommendation.body: Approve an incremental module layout only if the public served installer remains a single safe entrypoint and the website sync plus installer smoke matrix are updated in the same plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent installer-specific fixes and refactors make vincentkoc the best available owner for the installer split direction.
